pr_title: Update resource.AllocationResult with a slice of ResourceHandlers
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind feature
/kind api-change

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR is designed to resolve the following issue:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/115263

That is to say, it enables one to write a "meta" DRA resource driver that can allocate resources that are managed by multiple kubelet plugins. This becomes important, for example, when allocating topology-aligned resources from different vendors.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes #115263

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Action Required: Introduced a breaking change to the `resource.k8s.io` API in its `AllocationResult` struct. This change allows a kubelet plugin for the `DynamicResourceAllocation` feature to service allocations from multiple resource driver controllers.
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:
```docs
- [KEP]: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3802
```

issue_context.title: dynamic resource allocation: allow a kubelet-plugin to service allocations from multiple resource-driver controllers
issue_context.body: The goal is to allow one to write a custom controller such as the one below to (e.g.) co-allocate GPUs and RDMA interfaces (using a custom `ResourceClass` and associated `ClaimParameters` object), but allow the "default" kubelet-plugins for these resources to handle the actual device preparation and injection. **Note:** An older version of this description was too specific and suggested that we add an extension to the kubelet-plugin API to include an RCP called `WatchConfiguration`. Some of the comments at the beginning of this issue are in reference to that. We have since refined our thinking on how to do achieve the same goal, and those changes are reflected in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3802

I like the idea. One question so far:  Is my understanding correct that `WatchConfigurationResponse` is expected to always contain all supported driver names? This would allow to dynamically add and also remove names.

Yes, that is how it should be interpreted. Anytime the plugin has a new controller "register" with it, it should update the kubelet with a full list of driver names it supports. This list may grow or shrink over time (but it should always contain at least one entry -- the name of the "default" driver that it is associated with).

> it should always contain at least one entry -- the name of the "default" driver that it is associated with

From another point of view if plugin decides that for some reason it can't serve claims for the `ResourceClass`es with its default DriverName, it can remove default name from the list. We might want to allow this, but this is a minor detail.
Sure. I guess no matter what, the kubelet code should make sure to handle the case of an empty list being returned (though I assume this will almost never be the case).

In general, I pictured the kubelet code doing the following to support this:
1. Open a persistent watch on the new WatchConfiguration() call of each registered plugin
2. For each unique "driver name" (across all plugin configurations), maintain a list of all the plugins that should be triggered when a claim comes in that references that driver name
3. Update the code in the following to loop over all plugins associated with a claim referencing a given driver name:
     https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/manager.go#L110...L131
4. Concatenate the set of cdi devices passed back by each plugin into one

@klueska Can you give an example where we want to dynamically update the list of driver names for the plugin? I mean if plugin can handle different claim classes why wouldn't it just inform kubelet about it once?

The idea of making the list dynamic (via a watch) is just to allow new controllers to dynamically register themselves with a plugin after it is  already up and running (without needing to restart it).

The scenario would be:
1. Default GPU driver gets deployed (`gpu.resource.nvidia.com`)
2. Default RDMA driver gets deployed (`rdma.resource.nvidia.com`)
3. At this point any `ResourceClasses` that reference the `gpu.resource.nvidia.com` driver name will go through the controller associated with the default GPU driver, and any claims it allocates will eventually be serviced by the plugin associated with the default GPU driver.
4. Likewise, any `ResourceClasses` that reference the `rdma.resource.nvidia.com` driver name will go through the controller associated with the default RDMA driver, and any claims it allocates will eventually be serviced by the plugin associated with the default RDMA driver.
5. Once this is up and running, a new controller with driver name `custom.resource.nvidia.com` gets deployed. To allow its claim allocations to ultimately be serviced by both the default GPU driver's kubelet plugin and the default RDMA driver's kubelet plugin, it "registers" itself with these components so that they can update their lists of associated driver names with the kubelet (how this "registration" happens it out of scope of this feature, but would most likely be via a CRD).
6. At this point any `ResourceClasses` that reference the `custom.resource.nvidia.com` driver name will go through the new custom controller, and any claims it allocates will eventually be serviced by both the plugin associated with the default GPU driver and the plugin associated with the default RDMA driver.

It's not strictly necessary for custom controllers to dynamically "register" themselves with a plugin (e.g. one could supply a static list of supported driver names to a plugin via a command line flag). But I wanted to at least make the API to the kubelet support dynamism so that one would have the option to be more dynamic if they wanted.
